meta.name: Civil (linear works) 4D Programme Template
meta.what: Phase skeleton for a CIVIL model — every element's discipline is a CIVIL_DISCS code (import_worker.js). Selected by time_machine.js only when ALL elements are civil; building models keep 4D_template.json untouched (bim-compiler prompts/CIVIL_HIGHWAY_JELAPANG.md §Q, NON-IMPACT rule).
meta.order_source: secondary — JKR road-works method statements quoting JKR Standard Specification for Road Works (JKR/SPJ/2008): earthworks -> drainage -> pavement -> finishing (furniture, signage, lighting, marking). Primary document not yet read.
meta.durations: NOT civil-calibrated: one §CIVIL_TRADES crew per phase, params copied from MASON (what the proxy class gets today) so per-element durations are unchanged; finishing phases now run in parallel. Replace with JKR SoR / CIDB labour output.
meta.copied_from: 4D_template.json v1.2.0 — calendar, duration_rule, capacity_rule, phase_bands copied verbatim
meta.partner_discs: §PARTNER_DISCS (bim-compiler prompts/CIVIL_HIGHWAY_JELAPANG.md, 2026-10-06): setting_out, ground_treatment, slope_protection added from the BIM partner files; template sequence = list order (distinct), rates.js SEQUENCE_CIVIL sequence = cpm rank (grouped).

_placement_why: Civil finishing trades (furniture, signage, lighting, marking) all follow pavement and work on different parts of the road at once; with 'logic' each phase starts when its declared predecessor finishes (schedule_author.js §CIVIL_PARALLEL) instead of after the previous phase in the list.

calendar._what: The working calendar the programme is authored against. Named here because it was previously implicit: rates.js SHIFT_HOURS alone carried it, and nothing stated the week.
calendar._hours_per_shift_why: 24 is the STANDING USER RULING recorded at rates.js SHIFT_HOURS (2026-08-13): 'our default, import and JSON setting can import as we align to standard model'. Carried forward verbatim, NOT changed here — this file only makes it visible and editable. A standard-model import sets 8.
calendar._days_per_week_why: 7 matches what the engine actually does today (schedule_gate.js applies no week calendar; §CREW_DAY logs '24/7 calendar unchanged'). Stated so a 5-day working week becomes an edit rather than a rewrite.
calendar._project_start_why: §FUTURE-5A row B2 (2026-08-27 inventory, applied 2026-09-02, queue item B-3). The literal '2026-01-01' epoch schedule_author.js materializeZones/the §GANTT_SCHEDULE_STALE_REGEN self-heal path anchor a generated programme to when nothing else supplies a start. Extracted verbatim, not changed. NOT the same call site as the live UI's 'Generate Gantt' path (time_machine.js todayStart = new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10)) — that one is deliberately today's real date, out of this key's scope. 14 more '2026-01-01' sites exist in schedule_author_ui.js/schedule_diff.js/proj_control.js/proj_fold.js — outside this audit's scope (schedule_author.js/schedule_gate.js/time_machine.js scheduling call sites only), counted but not touched.

duration_rule._what: How an activity's duration is derived. THIS IS THE ANCHOR the chain was missing: before this, a task's length came from however long the geometry placement solve happened to span. The solve ORDERS elements; it does not PRICE the work.
duration_rule.formula: days = ceil( MAX over trades t of ( sum(installSecs of this activity's elements worked by t) / (hours_per_shift * 3600 * max_crews[t]) ) )
duration_rule._installSecs_source: ScheduleAuthor._installSecs, from sequence_rules.json LABOR_RATES productivity. Same function the engine uses — never a second copy.
duration_rule._max_crews_source: sequence_rules.json LABOR_RATES[trade].max_crews. Present on all 10 trades.
duration_rule._why_max_and_not_sum: v1.0.0 wrote 'crews = sum of max_crews over the trades the activity's own elements actually use' and divided the activity's TOTAL seconds by it. That treats trades as FUNGIBLE — an electrician's seconds worked off by a plumber's crew. Work content is per trade: an activity is as long as its slowest trade, never the pooled average. MEASURED on HHS_Office_Federated (6839 elements, 24h shift, 2026-08-25): whole-programme sum-of-crews = 40.1 days, correct per-trade = 69.8 days — the sum form understates by 1.74x overall, and up to 3.00x on a single phase (MEP Rough-in / MEP Final: 3 trades, Sum(max_crews)=6, but no one trade has more than 2 crews). The file exists to end a duration contradiction; the sum form would have replaced it with a new one.
duration_rule._same_bug_shipped_elsewhere: schedule_author.js materializeZones' §ZONE_WINDOW_COVERS_WORK floor computes _wCrews as the SAME sum. Any fix here is not complete until that site divides per trade too.
duration_rule._not_this: NOT the elapsed span of the placement solve.

capacity_rule._what: The hard physical bound on ANY schedule derived from this template. Distinct from duration_rule: duration_rule prices one activity, capacity_rule constrains the whole programme at every instant.
capacity_rule.rule: at no instant may more than max_crews[t] elements of trade t be in progress, for every trade t
capacity_rule.applies_to: the FINAL emitted times, not only the times at first placement
capacity_rule._why_final_and_not_first: MEASURED on HHS_Office_Federated (2026-08-25, A/B with the repair loop disabled): schedule_gate.js enforces the cap correctly inside claimCrew at placement — every trade sits exactly at or under its cap. The §DEQ_REPAIR sweep then moves elements forward to satisfy geometry gates by writing o.start/o.end DIRECTLY, without re-claiming a crew slot. Result: CARPENTER peaks at 8 simultaneous crews against max_crews=2, a 4.0x breach, while all 7 other trades stay legal. Disabling the repair loop returns CARPENTER to 2. The span is 46.9 days either way — the breach does not shorten the programme, it just makes it unbuildable.
capacity_rule._witness: witness_4d_capacity_honoured.js — sweeps the emitted start/end times per trade and asserts peak concurrency <= max_crews.
capacity_rule._level_scan_max_days_why: §FUTURE-5A row B6 (applied 2026-09-02, queue item B-3). instantiateTemplate's crew-levelling search guard (`while (!fits(t, at) && guard++ < LEVEL_SCAN_MAX) at++`) — how many days it will scan forward looking for a free crew slot before giving up. Extracted verbatim, not changed. ⚠ Separate finding #1 in §FUTURE-5A (NOT fixed here, PRIME-RULE-relevant but out of this refactor's scope): guard exhaustion is committed as if it were a successful placement, with no way to tell the two apart in `capacity_levelled`'s own report — moving the number does not touch that bug.

phases.name: Setting Out
phases._empty_ok_why: §PARTNER_DISCS: chainage labels / ROW boundary are setting-out references; a model without them is normal.

phases.name: Ground Treatment
phases._empty_ok_why: §PARTNER_DISCS: only projects with a GEOTECH file carry ground treatment.

phases.name: Earthworks
phases._empty_ok_why: The old export carried an empty TIN-only earthwork file; the partner re-export (2026-10-05) carries the earthworks body as one solid. Absence is still allowed and reported.

phases.name: Slope Protection
phases._empty_ok_why: §PARTNER_DISCS: gabion mattress where the design calls for it.

phase_bands._what: A phase owns a CONTIGUOUS, NON-OVERLAPPING band of sequence_rules.json sequence numbers. Declared as a rule, not as a list, because the numbers themselves live in the lookup.
phase_bands.rule: max(sequence of every class in phase[i]) < min(sequence of every class in phase[i+1])
phase_bands._why: v1.0.0 gated only that each phase's MINIMUM sequence increases. That cannot see a band INTERLEAVE — the exact defect §S65 #7 found and PR #1527 fixed (IfcRoof sat at sequence 8, inside Architecture, therefore after ALL of MEP Rough-in at 7). Under a min-only gate Architecture's min stays 5, the mins still increase, and the witness stays green while a roof is built after the ductwork it is supposed to cover. Bands MEASURED clean 2026-08-25: Substructure 1-1, Superstructure 2-4, Architecture 5-6, MEP Rough-in 7-7, MEP Final 9-9, Finishes 10-11.

dependencies._what: Civil logic (secondary source, see meta.order_source). Finishing trades all follow pavement and run in parallel.

within_level._why: Set out the corridor (chainage, right-of-way) before any works.
Piles / soil nails carry the embankment — installed before the fill they support.
Drains are cut into the formed earthworks.
Cross drainage / culverts before pavement layers.
Marking on the final wearing course.
Gabion mattress on the formed slopes / outlets.
Slope protection in place before pavement works.
